title: Describe Image (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), ML Model, Vision)
cap_description: Generate detailed image descriptions using GGUF multimodal models (LLaVA, BakLLaVA) with llama.cpp backend
documentation:
## Purpose

Generates detailed, instruction-following natural-language descriptions of PNG images using GGUF multimodal (vision-language) models via llama.cpp. Supports models like moondream2, LLaVA, and BakLLaVA. The prompt can ask specific questions about image content.

## Inputs

- A GGUF vision model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `moondream2-20250414-GGUF`.
- A PNG image file.
- A text prompt (default: "Describe this image in detail."). Customize to ask specific questions.
- Max tokens (default 256) and temperature (default 0.6).

## Outputs

A text description of the image as a plain string.

## Notes

- Vision-language models follow instructions in the prompt, making them more flexible than BLIP-style captioning models.
- Lower temperature (0.3-0.5) produces more factual, less creative descriptions.
- For Apple Silicon, prefer [Describe Image (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:image;png";ml-model;mlx;op=describe_image;out="media:image-description;textable";vision) for better performance.
- Input must be PNG.

## Backend
The inference framework or runtime that loads and executes a model. Backend choice
determines weight format, hardware acceleration, and runtime characteristics. A media
URN that omits the backend tag is backend-agnostic — it accepts any backend.

GGUF is the llama.cpp container format. Quantised weights packaged into a single
file with embedded metadata. Runs efficiently on CPU and via Metal/CUDA acceleration.
Standard format for general-purpose LLM and embedding inference across hardware.

## ML model
Marker indicating the cap invokes a machine-learning model. Inputs typically
include a model spec or model artifact; the cap is subject to model-resolution
and hardware-pressure policies.

The cap invokes a machine-learning model.

## Model task
The inference modality of a model. Model-task narrows what kind of inference cap a
model spec is suitable for: an LLM cannot serve transcription, a transcription model
cannot serve text generation. The task tag is part of the model-spec URN; it is set
by the cap declaring its model-spec input slot, not derived from the model file.

Vision-language model for image captioning, visual question answering, and other
multimodal tasks. Accepts text and images, produces text.
